name: Chamonix

seo.title: Chamonix ski resort guide
seo.description: A valley of separate ski sectors under Mont Blanc, from Brévent at 2,525 m to the Aiguille du Midi cable car at 3,842 m.
seo.twitterDescription: Separate sectors under Mont Blanc, up to 3,842 metres.
seo.webpageDescription: Ski facts, where to stay and how to get to Chamonix in Haute-Savoie.

h1: Chamonix ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Chamonix is not one linked mountain but a valley of separate sectors, each with its own cable car: Brévent at 2,525 metres, Flégère at 2,396, Balme at 2,270 above Le Tour and Vallorcine, and Grands Montets at 2,765 above Argentière. Over all of them the Aiguille du Midi climbs to 3,842 metres, the starting point for the off-piste descents the valley is known for.
stayOverview: The town sits in the valley floor under Mont Blanc, with Brévent and the Aiguille du Midi leaving from its edges. Argentière is the village up the valley under Grands Montets; Les Houches is down the other way.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. Chamonix town is the one with the life; Argentière and Les Houches sit under their own mountains.
rentalCars: Chamonix is at the French mouth of the Mont Blanc tunnel, about an hour from Geneva.

lifts.value: 2 cable cars, 7 gondolas, 14 chairlifts and 21 ski lifts
lifts.note: The operator publishes the breakdown for the Chamonix Le Pass area but no total, and adding them up would be our arithmetic rather than its figure.
lifts.sourceLabel: Mont-Blanc Natural Resort: CHAMONIX Le Pass

verticalDrop.unannounced: No vertical drop is published for any of the Chamonix sectors.

topElevation.note: The highest of the valley’s pisted sectors, at Grands Montets. Our figure, taken from the sector altitudes the operator publishes - it states none for the valley as a whole. The Aiguille du Midi reaches 3,842 m but is an excursion cable car serving off-piste, not a pisted sector.

season.note: The Chamonix Le Pass period, which covers Grands Montets, Balme and Brévent/Flégère. Each sector runs its own dates; Grands Montets goes on to 2 May.

snowpark.note: On the Brévent side: five rails and a giant airbag, with ESF instructors on hand.

pistes.value: 98 km on the Chamonix Le Pass area
pistes.sourceLabel: Mont-Blanc Natural Resort: CHAMONIX Le Pass

baseElevation.note: The lowest base the operator publishes for any Chamonix sector. Les Houches - Saint-Gervais runs 1,000 to 1,900 m; Grands Montets starts at 1,235 m. Our choice among the operator's own sector figures - it states no single base for the valley.

longestRun.unannounced: The lift company publishes each Chamonix sector's altitudes, lifts and piste kilometres separately - the valley is not one ski area - but no run length, and names no longest run.
longestRun.sourceLabel: Mont-Blanc Natural Resort: CHAMONIX Le Pass

dayPass.note: The range the lift company publishes for a one-day Chamonix Le Pass across its three 2026/27 periods - 28 November to 18 December 2026, 19 December to 9 April 2027 and 10 April to 2 May 2027 - without saying which price belongs to which period. Le Pass covers Brévent-Flégère, Grands Montets and Balme.

sectors.name: Brévent - Flégère
sectors.summary: 28 Nov 2026 - 18 Apr 2027, topping out at 2,525 m
sectors.text: The sunny side of the valley, facing Mont Blanc, bordering the nature reserve. Brévent is reached from the centre of Chamonix, Flégère by cable car from Les Praz three kilometres away.

rows.label: Freestyle
rows.value: Five rails and a giant airbag at the Teleski 2000, on the Brévent side

rows.label: Speed run
rows.value: The timed Chavanne speed piste, on the Flégère side

rows.label: Beginners
rows.value: The Savoy area at 1,877 m, at the foot of the resort

sectors.name: Grands Montets
sectors.summary: 28 Nov 2026 - 2 May 2027, the valley’s longest season
sectors.text: The operator calls it the mecca of skiing: vertiginous drops right beside the glaciers.

rows.label: The new lift
rows.value: A detachable 3S gondola from Lognan to the summit, above 3,000 m

sectors.name: Balme - Vallorcine
sectors.text: The wild end of the valley at the Swiss border, reached from the old village of Le Tour - 11 km from Chamonix - and from Vallorcine.

rows.label: Getting up
rows.value: The Charamillon gondola from Le Tour, or Vallorcine’s own

sectors.name: Les Houches - Saint-Gervais
sectors.text: The wooded, lower end of the valley, and the one the families use - though it also holds the World Cup downhill.

rows.label: The Verte des Houches
rows.value: The World Cup downhill the sector is known for

rows.label: Getting up
rows.value: The Bellevue cable car and the Prarion gondola

sectors.summary: 3,842 m - excursion cable car, off-piste only
sectors.text: Not a pisted sector but an excursion cable car, and the way into the off-piste descents the valley is known for.
